tools.name: image.generate
tools.description: Generate one to four images from a text prompt, optionally guided by one reference image.

prompt.description: What to draw. Everything about the image comes from this text.
examples: a paper boat on a rain-soaked street at night

image_key.description: Optional reference image, given as the id of an upload you confirmed or of an artifact from an earlier job. The result follows its subject and composition.

count.description: How many images to generate. Each one is charged.

tools.name: image.ltt
tools.description: Generate images with LTT Studios' own model. Supports text-to-image, instruction editing of a reference image, and keeping the same subject across a new scene.

prompt.description: What to draw. Written in any language - the platform translates it to English before the model sees it, because this model only understands English and Chinese. Text you want DRAWN INSIDE the image must be in double quotes; it is kept exactly as written.
examples: A calico cat sleeping on a windowsill, afternoon light

mode.description: t2i = from text only. edit = change one reference image while keeping the rest. subject = keep the same person or object across a new scene. edit and subject both need image_key and both cost three times more because they take about three times as long; t2i refuses a reference image.

count.description: How many images to return, 1 to 4.

image_key.description: Reference image, given as the id of an upload you confirmed or of an artifact from an earlier job. Required for edit and subject. Sending it with t2i is REJECTED, not ignored.

tools.name: image.thumbnail
tools.description: Generate one to four YouTube thumbnail background images from a topic. The images carry NO text: the internal model cannot render legible lettering, so add your own title afterwards.

topic.description: What the thumbnail is about. The whole image is generated from this, so be specific about subject and mood.
examples: How to fix a leaking tap in 5 minutes

phong_cach.description: Visual style of the image itself. The name is Vietnamese because it is a stable identifier, not a label; the values are listed in `enum`.

kieu_trend.description: Composition pattern — what makes the thumbnail work as a thumbnail (a reacting face, a before/after split, a mystery crop, and so on).

aspect_ratio.description: Shape of the output. 16:9 is the YouTube thumbnail shape.

count.description: How many variations to generate. Each one is charged, so a quote for count=4 costs four times a quote for count=1.

tools.name: image.upscale
tools.description: Upscale an image to four times its original size. Costs 2 credits at the fast preset and 4 at the quality preset.

image_key.description: The image to enlarge, given as the id of an upload you confirmed or of an artifact from an earlier job.

preset.description: How hard to work on the result. `fast` costs 2 credits, `quality` costs 4 and takes longer.

tools.name: speech.ltt
tools.description: Turn Vietnamese or English text into natural speech. Use a built-in preset voice, or one of your own cloned voices by its stable voice id.

text.description: What to say. Vietnamese, English, or both mixed. Up to 100,000 characters per call. You do NOT need to split long text yourself - it is segmented on sentence boundaries, spoken in several passes and joined back into one continuous audio file. For anything longer, use Projects, where each block is its own pass.
examples: Xin chào, đây là giọng đọc của LTT Studios.

voice_id.description: One of your own cloned voices, as returned when you created it. Stays valid across engine upgrades. Leave empty to use a built-in voice.

preset.description: A built-in voice name. Ignored when voice_id is given; sending both is rejected.

tools.name: story.storyboard
tools.description: Turn a story brief into a storyboard: one shot description per scene plus a master prompt. Priced by scene count.

title.description: Working title of the piece. Used for tone and for naming the result.

story.description: The story or brief, in prose. This is the source everything else is derived from.
examples: A courier misses the last train and walks the city until dawn.

scene_count.description: How many scenes to produce. This is what the price depends on.

aspect_ratio.description: Shape the scenes are written for; it changes framing advice, not the file.

style.description: Visual or narrative style to aim for, in your own words.

tools.name: text.chat
tools.description: Generate text from a conversation. Handles coding, chat, agentic tool use, summarisation and image reading. OpenAI-compatible message format.

messages.description: Conversation so far, OpenAI format: a list of {role, content}. `content` may be a string, or a list of parts for images.

model.description: `ltt_llm` for text (156K usable input context). `ltt_llm_vision` also reads images, with a smaller 89K input context.

max_tokens.description: Ceiling on generated tokens. Credit is held against this and refunded down to what was actually generated.

tools.description: Function definitions, OpenAI format. The model may answer with `tool_calls`.

reasoning_effort.description: How much the model thinks before answering. Deeper costs more output tokens.

tools.name: text.prompt_package
tools.description: Turn a story brief into a structured prompt package: one prompt per scene plus a master prompt. Priced by scene count.

title.description: Working title of the piece. Used for tone and for naming the result.

story.description: The story or brief, in prose. This is the source everything else is derived from.
examples: A courier misses the last train and walks the city until dawn.

scene_count.description: How many scenes to produce. This is what the price depends on.

duration_seconds.description: Target length of the finished piece. Scenes are paced to fit it.

aspect_ratio.description: Shape the scenes are written for; it changes framing advice, not the file.

style.description: Visual or narrative style to aim for, in your own words.

examples: people who commute late at night

language.description: Language the prompts are written in.

tools.name: video.generate
tools.description: Generate video from a text prompt, optionally guided by reference media. Valid resolution, duration and aspect ratio depend on the model — see each model's `constraints` in GET /api/v1/models.

prompt.description: What the video should show. Write it in any language; longer and more specific prompts give steadier results than short ones.
examples: A calico cat stretching on a sunlit windowsill

model.description: Which model renders the video. Each one accepts a different set of resolutions and durations — see GET /api/v1/models.

resolution.description: Output resolution. Valid values depend on the model — read `constraints.resolutions` for the model you picked. Higher costs more.

duration.description: Video length in **seconds**, not frames. Valid values depend on the model — read `constraints.durations`. Price scales with it.

aspect_ratio.description: Frame shape. Valid values depend on the model — read `constraints.aspect_ratios`.

generate_audio.description: Whether the model also generates a soundtrack. Leave it on unless you are supplying your own.

camera.description: Camera movement. Empty means the model decides.

motion.description: How much the subject moves. Empty means default.

visual_style.description: Overall look. Empty means the model follows the prompt alone.

seed.description: Repeat a previous result. The same seed with the same input gives the same video; omit it for a new one each time.

image_key.description: Upload id of one reference image to guide the first frame. Optional.

tools.name: video.subtitle
tools.description: Burn a transcript you already have into a video as styled subtitles. Costs 5 credits per minute at standard quality; draft costs 0.6x and high costs 1.5x. The duration is measured from the file you upload, not from anything you send.

video_key.description: The video to subtitle, given as the id of an upload you confirmed or of an artifact from an earlier job.

transcript.description: The words to burn in, as a list of segments with `start`, `end` and `text`. This tool does not transcribe for you.

style_id.description: Look of the subtitles: font, colour and outline. Does not change the price.

segment_mode.description: How the transcript is cut into on-screen lines — whole sentences, shorter phrases, or one emphasised word at a time.

quality.description: Encoding quality of the finished video. `draft` costs 0.6 times the standard price and `high` costs 1.5 times.

output_format.description: Container of the finished video file.

export_srt.description: Also return the subtitles as a separate .srt file alongside the video.

tools.name: video.upscale
tools.description: Upscale a video to 1080p, 1440p or 4K. Costs 30 credits per minute at 1080p on the fast preset; 1440p costs 1.8x, 4K costs 4x, and the quality preset costs 2.5x. The duration is measured from the file you upload, not from anything you send.

video_key.description: The video to enlarge, given as the id of an upload you confirmed or of an artifact from an earlier job.

preset.description: How hard to work on the result. `quality` costs 2.5 times as much as `fast` and takes longer.

target_height.description: Height of the finished video in pixels. 1440 costs 1.8 times the 1080 price and 2160 costs 4 times.

codec.description: Video codec of the finished file. `hevc` makes a smaller file that fewer players open.

preview.description: Render only the first 8 seconds, and charge only for them. Use it to check the settings before paying for the whole video.

preserve_fps.description: Keep the original frame rate instead of letting the encoder choose one.

preserve_audio.description: Copy the original audio track across.

stabilize.description: Reduce camera shake. Costs 1.2 times the price without it.

smooth_motion.description: Interpolate frames for smoother motion. Costs 2.2 times the price without it, and combines with `stabilize`.
